claims.text: The FDA label reports no clinically important potentiation of alcohol's pharmacodynamic effects by tiagabine.
claims.quote: Tiagabine has shown no clinically important potentiation of the pharmacodynamic effects of triazolam or alcohol.

claims.text: The FDA label also flags possible additive nervous system depressant effects with tiagabine and ethanol.
claims.quote: Because of the possible additive effects of drugs that may depress the nervous system, ethanol or triazolam should be used cautiously in combination with tiagabine.

claims.text: A double-blind study found no pharmacodynamic interaction between tiagabine and ethanol on the measured cognitive, motor, and subjective variables.
claims.quote: There was no evidence of a pharmacodynamic interaction between tiagabine and ethanol with respect to these variables.

claims.text: The same study found unchanged pharmacokinetic parameters for tiagabine and ethanol during combined administration.
claims.quote: The pharmacokinetic parameters of tiagabine and ethanol (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax], time to Cmax and area under the plasma concentration-time curve) were unchanged during concomitant administration.

headline.text: The FDA label reports no clinically important alcohol potentiation by tiagabine, while noting possible additive nervous system effects.

reported.text: A double-blind study found no interaction on its measured cognitive, motor, and subjective variables.
Tiagabine and ethanol pharmacokinetic parameters were unchanged during combined administration.
